A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DisCa work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material. Retained content can be matched reliably despite added experiments and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original HunyuanVideo experiments, including VBench scores, acceleration and memory measurements, component ablations, and generated-video examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds HunyuanVideo 1.5 image-to-video experiments, user preferences, a distillation ablation, and semantic-subscore analysis.

M1.justification: The Restricted MeanFlow restriction, learnable predictor, caching procedure, adversarial losses, and Algorithms 1–3 are retained. The image-to-video evaluation and additional ablation introduce no documented revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates text-to-video generation on HunyuanVideo. v3 additionally evaluates image-to-video generation on HunyuanVideo 1.5 using 300 selected image-text pairs (Section 7.1), substantially extending coverage to image-conditioned generation.

E2.justification: MagCache, AdaCache, and DCM, previously cited but not experimentally compared, become evaluated comparators alongside TaylorSeer in v3 Table 4 and Figure 6. The original text-to-video comparator suite is retained.

E3.justification: The added image-to-video experiment evaluates four and eight NFE using LPIPS, PSNR, and SSIM against non-accelerated outputs on 300 pairs. Separate four-step and eight-step user-preference comparisons are also introduced. These substantially expand the evaluation design; the existing VBench protocol is unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 Table 5 adds comparisons with a predictor operating without distillation, whereas v1 Table 3 compares ordinary versus Restricted MeanFlow and removes caching or GAN components. v3 also adds a nine-category semantic-score breakdown (Table 6), revealing strengths and failures concealed by aggregate scores.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added user-preference percentages and benchmark scores remain point estimates without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–3 and the timing table, renumbered from Table 4 to Table 7, retain their numerical results. v3 adds substantial results in Tables 4–6 and Figure 6: for example, four-NFE DisCa achieves LPIPS 0.1942, PSNR 19.29, and SSIM 0.7071, and receives 74.7% preference in the four-step panel. These are newly reported experiments, not improvements to previously reported same-setting scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1–8, and associated reasoning are retained. No new formal assumption, proof, derivation, or theorem accompanies the additional experiments.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: distillation-compatible learnable caching, conservative Restricted MeanFlow, and approximately lossless acceleration up to 11.8 times. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 7.3 newly attributes distillation benefits to smoother trajectories. Section 7.2 acknowledges a remaining gap against non-accelerated generation, while Section 8.3 interprets improved spatial relationships and identifies scene degradation as a limitation requiring future work.

D1.justification: v1 states that code is in supplementary materials and will become public; v3 supplies a specific repository link in the abstract. This makes access information more concrete. Existing hardware, training hyperparameters, iteration counts, and pseudocode are retained.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography retain the same works and substantive positioning. MagCache, AdaCache, DCM, and HunyuanVideo 1.5 were already cited in v1; their new experimental use does not introduce a revised novelty argument.

P1.justification: v3 adds acknowledgments, author contact information, a supplementary-experiments section, and a semantic-breakdown subsection, with corresponding renumbering and a short main-text pointer. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds three appendix tables and a two-panel user-preference pie chart, producing localized layout changes. The original timing table and appendix figures are retained and renumbered; existing diagrams and visual examples are unchanged, with minor table-header and placement adjustments.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's text-to-video-only evidence, v3 adds useful image-to-video comparisons and makes a previously hidden scene-quality weakness explicit. These improve empirical coverage and transparency. The gains are limited by sparse documentation of the new evaluation and user-study procedures, absent uncertainty estimates, and mixed eight-NFE ablation results: the undistilled predictor has better PSNR and SSIM than Restricted MeanFlow in Table 5. Overall, the additions provide a useful but qualified quality improvement.
